idea-plugin.name: Claude Relay
idea-plugin.description:
Claude Relay — Claude Code, native in your JetBrains IDE

A native chat panel that drives the official Claude Code CLI from inside IntelliJ IDEA, PyCharm, WebStorm, GoLand, Rider and the rest of the JetBrains family — the side-panel experience you'd get in VS Code, without leaving your IDE or living in the terminal.

Highlights

  • Streaming chat with live tool activity — edits, commands, and file reads as they happen
  • Agent & Ask modes — let Claude edit and run commands, or keep it strictly read-only
  • Editor-aware — auto-attaches your current selection, so "explain/refactor this" just works
  • Attach files & images — pick a file, or paste a screenshot straight into the prompt
  • Project context — picks up your CLAUDE.md, agents, skills and slash commands automatically
  • Session history — resume past conversations from a built-in picker
  • Model & permission selectors, with live usage and limits

Requires the Claude Code CLI installed separately (npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code) and an active Claude subscription.

☕ Free and open source (MIT). Source, issues, and contributions: github.com/Chelayel/claude-relay.

Independent and unofficial — not affiliated with Anthropic. Part of the “Relay” family of IDE companions by Chelayel.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.0.17 — Questions now work. When Claude wanted to ask a multiple-choice question it used its interactive picker, which has no UI in the CLI's headless mode and auto-resolved to “no answer was selected.” Claude now asks in plain text instead, so you can just type your answer.

1.0.15 — Restored the rich chat transcript on IntelliJ 2026.2+ (build 262), where JCEF became a separate bundled plugin — the panel now depends on it optionally so the in-browser view works again instead of dropping to plain text. The plain-text fallback also renders at the correct font size when JCEF isn't available.

1.0.14 — Fixed oversized text in the plain-text transcript fallback (used when JCEF isn't available): it now renders at the IDE's UI font size instead of an inflated one.

1.0.13 — Fixed the tool window failing to open on recent IntelliJ builds (NoClassDefFoundError: com/intellij/ui/jcef/JBCefApp). When JCEF isn't available on the plugin classpath the panel now falls back to the plain-text transcript instead of failing to initialize.

1.0.12 — Compatibility fix for upcoming IntelliJ releases (replaced a platform API scheduled for removal in the popup choosers).

1.0.11 — Much lower token usage in longer chats: each conversation now runs through a single persistent Claude Code session, keeping the prompt cache warm across turns instead of re-sending the whole transcript every message.

1.0.10 — The tool-window icon now uses the Claude accent red so it matches the plugin icon instead of looking washed-out in dark themes.

1.0.9 — Reliability fix: the model picker no longer gets stuck on the bare fallback list when the /model scrape races a slow CLI start-up; it now waits longer and retries. Added diagnostic logging for picker issues.

1.0.8 — New Auto-Test to Coverage toolbar action: pick a target line-coverage percentage and Claude keeps writing and running unit tests until it reaches it. The model picker now shows the concrete Claude version for each choice (e.g. Opus 4.8, Sonnet 4.6, Haiku 4.5).

1.0.7 — New original plugin logo. The context bar “Rescan” button now has a distinct icon so it’s no longer confused with the toolbar “Refresh”. Additional compatibility fix for upcoming IntelliJ releases (replaced another platform API scheduled for removal).

1.0.3 — Compatibility fix for upcoming IntelliJ releases (replaced a platform API scheduled for removal). Shift+Enter inserts a newline.

1.0.2 — Claude Relay is now free and open source (MIT). Source & contributions: github.com/Chelayel/claude-relay.

1.0.1 — Fixed intermittent “Project context” bar visibility.

1.0.0 — First release: native Claude Code chat panel with streaming transcript & tool activity, Agent & Ask modes, single-select agent persona, editor-aware context, file & image attachments, project agents/skills/commands, session history, and model/permission selectors.
